messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

output:
Placeholders in brackets — swap in your own names, dates, and numbers. I invented the latency and window figures as examples; replace them or cut the claims.

---

**Subject: [Service] moves to [New Platform] in [Q4]**

Short version: your account, your data, and your integrations come with you. Nothing to rebuild.

Here's what's happening. On [date], [Service] moves off [Old Platform] and onto [New Platform]. We've run both in parallel since [month] and the new stack has held: median API response dropped from 340 ms to 90 ms, and we can ship [feature] without waiting on a six-week release train.

**What you need to do**

Before [date] — nothing. We migrate accounts in batches and email each one 14 days ahead, then again that morning.

After — point your calls at `[new-endpoint]`. The old endpoint keeps answering until [sunset date], then returns a permanent redirect. If you run self-hosted connectors, upgrade to [version] first.

**Downtime**

One window: [date], 02:00–04:00 UTC. Reads stay up the whole time. Writes queue and flush when we're back.

**What doesn't change**

Pricing. Contract terms. Support response times. Your retention settings, your roles, your audit history.

**What does**

[Old feature] retires — [replacement] does the same job with a different config screen. Webhook payloads gain two fields; existing parsers won't break.

Live status during the move at [status URL]. If your team can't take that window — quarter-end close, a launch, an audit — reply here and we'll schedule you separately. No penalty, no form.

Questions to [email]. A person reads that inbox.

— [Name], [Title]
